official_measurement_examples.name: SPZ non-statutory map status
official_measurement_examples.fact: Environment Agency guidance describes SPZs as non-statutory mapped protection zones used to manage groundwater pollution risk; being in an SPZ is not by itself a planning refusal or planning permission.

official_measurement_examples.name: SPZ1 definition
official_measurement_examples.fact: SPZ1 is the inner protection zone around drinking-water abstraction sources and uses the larger of statutory distance or travel-time criteria where applicable; it must not be inferred from a generic buffer alone.

official_measurement_examples.name: SPZ2 and SPZ3 separation
official_measurement_examples.fact: SPZ2 is an outer protection zone using distance/travel-time criteria, while SPZ3 represents the total source catchment; the zones are not interchangeable risk classes.

official_measurement_examples.name: Permit interaction
official_measurement_examples.fact: Activities in SPZs can face stricter environmental-permitting and risk-assessment requirements, but an SPZ map does not itself prove whether a specific activity is permitted or prohibited without checking the applicable rules.

official_measurement_examples.name: Sewage threshold interaction
official_measurement_examples.fact: Environmental-permit risk guidance uses different treated-sewage thresholds inside and outside SPZ1; these thresholds are permit-assessment rules and not parcel development-capacity values.

official_measurement_examples.name: Landfill sensitivity
official_measurement_examples.fact: Environment Agency landfill guidance normally objects to inert landfill in SPZ1 and requires additional hydrogeological evidence in SPZ2/3; this is activity-specific and not a universal ban on all development.

official_measurement_examples.name: 2026 groundwater guidance currentity
official_measurement_examples.fact: The Groundwater protection in England collection was updated 21 April 2026 and current permit guidance in 2026 must be retained separately from older SPZ mapping methodology dates.

official_measurement_examples.name: Parcel limitation
official_measurement_examples.fact: SPZ presence does not determine title, planning permission, exact buildable area, drainage feasibility or final development yield without proposal-specific evidence.

core_rules: SPZ is non-statutory risk zoning not planning designation
SPZ presence is not automatic planning refusal
SPZ absence is not proof of no groundwater risk
mapped zone is not exact hydrogeological site investigation
sewage thresholds are not development-capacity values
landfill restrictions do not generalise to all development
planning permission does not replace environmental permit
environmental permit does not prove planning permission
SPZ does not calculate parcel yield
guidance date and map lineage must remain distinct
no parcel groundwater clearance or Future Growth score may be promoted while recovery is parked
source_verification_note: Official Environment Agency, Defra, GOV.UK and legislation sources checked 2026-07-26. April-May 2026 groundwater/permitting guidance currentity retained with SPZ1/2/3, activity-specific permitting and planning separation; no parcel promotion.
